content.heading: Begin with nutrition, then follow your signals
content.intro: Fine Diet programs are built with care to help you stabilize first, personalize second, and avoid unnecessary restriction. You’ll begin with the 21-Day Baseline, complete guided check-ins, and move into the next program based on your patterns.
content.ctaNote: Every program is designed to work with your Fine Diet journal—not outside of it. You’ll plan meals, track body feedback, complete check-ins, and build a clearer path from “what am I doing?” to “this is what works for me.”

content.heading: A simple sequence for finding your baseline.
content.intro: This module preserves the current page idea in an editable form: start with nutrition, learn from the signals, and move only when the next step is useful.

steps.title: Start with Baseline
steps.body: Build a practical nutrition rhythm before chasing more complexity.

steps.title: Watch your signals
steps.body: Use the app and journal to notice what changes across meals, energy, digestion, and routines.

steps.title: Choose the next pathway
steps.body: Move into focused program work when the pattern is clear enough to act on.

steps.title: Keep what works
steps.body: Protect the habits that improve your day-to-day life instead of restarting again.

content.heading: Meet your nutrition foundations
content.subhead: This resolver-driven module keeps program sequence cards tied to the Programs catalogue instead of editable module copy.

content.text: NOT A DETOX. NOT A DIET CHALLENGE. NOT ANOTHER TRACKER.

items.question: What are these public Programs pages for?
items.answer: They explain the pathway and help you choose where to begin. Active enrollment, delivery, and access happen in the Fine Diet app.

items.question: Where should most people start?
items.answer: Most members should begin with Baseline in Nutrition Foundations, then move into focused pathways when their signals point to a useful next step.

items.question: Can module copy change program access or pricing?
items.answer: No. Modules are presentation surfaces. Pricing, checkout, trial enforcement, grants, and entitlement truth stay outside module content.
